findings.summary: THE ID M0.65 IS REUSED FOR A SECOND, UNRELATED TASK. M0.65 is already an OPEN row: backlog.md:34 and backlog-notes.md:47-49 carry `CommitLog` holds TWO states for one fact ... setting `sealedAt` at the lost-race site (Serves FR-11, state todo). The diff files the review-tree process leak under the same ID, and adds a SECOND `### M0.65` heading to backlog-notes.md at line 331. sdd.md rule 4 states 'Task IDs are stable and never reused. Format M<n>.<k>.' and backlog.md's own line 10 repeats it: 'IDs are stable and never reused.' sdd.md is one of the two standards this packet selected for the change, so the rule is in scope by the packet's own routing. `### M0.65` is now the only duplicated heading in backlog-notes.md (verified: `grep -n '^### ' | sort | uniq -d` yields exactly M0.65). The M0 space is contiguous through M0.74 across backlog.md and backlog-done.md with M0.75 free, so an unused ID was available at zero cost.
findings.failure_scenario: Three concrete failures, none of them visible to a gate. (1) THE NEW ROW'S OWN NOTES LINK GOES TO THE WRONG BODY. Two `### M0.65` headings render as `#m065` and `#m065-1`, so `[notes](backlog-notes.md#m065)` on the NEW backlog.md:147 row lands on the CommitLog `sealedAt` notes at line 49, not on the leak notes at line 333. A session that picks the leak row and follows its own link -- which AGENTS.md instructs it to do, 'Read the notes for the ONE task you pick' -- reads the notes for a different task and starts writing the wrong change. check-links.sh cannot see this: it strips the fragment before resolving (`t="${l%%#*}"`, scripts/check-links.sh:34) and checks only that the FILE exists, which it does. (2) THE COMMIT-MSG GATE CANNOT TELL THEM APART. check-commit-msg.sh requires only that the subject start with an ID present in the backlog, so `M0.65: reap the processes a finished reviewer leaves` and `M0.65: set sealedAt at the lost-race site` are both accepted; whichever lands first, moving 'the' M0.65 row to backlog-done.md silently orphans the other, and non-negotiable 1's one-task-one-commit property no longer holds for this ID. (3) REPORTING BREAKS. AGENTS.md's Never section forbids naming an ID that does not RESOLVE; M0.65 now resolves to two different tasks, so no report using it can be unambiguous. Fix: renumber the new row to M0.75 in backlog.md, in the notes heading, and in its `[notes]` anchor.

findings.summary: THE NOT-A-SWEEP CLAUSE ATTRIBUTES A MEASUREMENT TO M0.74 THAT M0.74 DOES NOT RECORD. The new row says: 'M0.74's row records that an age-based `rm -rf` was measured destroying a live reviewer's tree mid-review, and the same hazard applies to killing by age.' M0.74's row, backlog-notes.md:245, says something different: 'review-tree.sh's history is that the `rm -rf` was the dangerous part, an earlier draft having been measured destroying a live reviewer's tree mid-review, and an age-based sweep puts it back.' The measured destruction is attributed there to 'an earlier draft', and an age-based sweep is the HYPOTHETICAL that would reintroduce it -- never a measured event. scripts/review-tree.sh's own header settles what that earlier draft was: 'An earlier draft keyed the path on repository+role and `rm -rf`'d it first; round-1 review measured its own tree being removed and re-created underneath it mid-review by an unrelated invocation for the same role.' Path-keyed, not age-based. So the row converts a refused hypothesis into a recorded measurement and cites a source that says the opposite of what is claimed. THE CLAUSE'S CONCLUSION IS SOUND -- M0.74 does refuse an age-based sweep, review-tree.sh repeats the refusal in the block that prints the tree count, and 'reap what a KNOWN-FINISHED agent left, or report past a threshold' is the right shape and mirrors what the script actually does today (find/wc -l, threshold 40, no removal). What is wrong is one clause of evidence, and the fix is one clause: 'M0.74's row refuses an age-based sweep on the ground that an earlier draft's `rm -rf` was measured destroying a live reviewer's tree mid-review'.
findings.failure_scenario: This row exists to steer a future implementer away from a reaper that kills by age. That implementer does the right thing -- checks the cited source before accepting a constraint that rules out the obvious implementation -- reads M0.74's row and review-tree.sh's header, finds no age-based sweep was ever measured destroying anything, concludes the NOT A SWEEP clause is overstated, and writes the age-based reaper. It then kills the JVM of a live reviewer whose build has been running longer than the threshold, and the reviewer reports a suite failure it cannot reproduce -- the same class of evidence corruption this very row is filed about, reinstated by a false citation inside the row that was supposed to prevent it. Second-order: this is non-negotiable 4's failure mode ('never claim ... a number was measured, without having done it') appearing inside the row whose entire subject is measurements taken under conditions that were not what they seemed.

findings.summary: THE HARNESS ROW IS FILED IN THE M4 SECTION, NOT THE M0 SECTION. backlog.md has four milestone sections (M0 harness at line 16, M1 at 67, M2 at 95, M4 at 107). The new M0.65 row is appended at line 147, between M4.44 and M4.15, i.e. inside `## M4 -- sequencer and commit log`. It is a harness task -- it names `scripts/review-tree.sh` and M0.74, carries `--` in Serves, and every other M0.x row in the file sits under `## M0 -- harness`. The sibling row added in the same diff, M4.45, is correctly placed. This travels with R-M0.65-1: renumbering to M0.75 and moving it into the M0 section are one edit.
findings.failure_scenario: A session working the current milestone reads the M4 section as its task list -- backlog.md's preamble names M4 as the current milestone -- and picks a harness task that has nothing to do with sequencing, or skips it as mis-scoped and never returns. A session doing harness work reads the M0 section and never sees the row at all, so the leak stays unfixed and the next round of timing measurements is taken under it again. No gate reads the section headings, so nothing else catches this.

findings.summary: TWO FIGURES ARE PRESENTED AS QUOTATIONS THAT THE ARTIFACTS DO NOT CARRY, AND ONE COUNT CONTRADICTS ANOTHER. What I could verify in `.harness/review/`: 'load average 123' and 'load average 186' appear verbatim in recorded verdicts; 'cannot flake on a loaded machine' appears verbatim; the honest 6-7 renew-rate values appear ('6 (three idle runs), 6 (two runs under 32 spinners on 20 cores), 7 (two runs at load average 123)', and 'load average ~206) and got fast=6, fast=7, fast=7'). What I could NOT verify: the quoted '206-213' -- the string does not occur anywhere under `.harness/`, and the closest recorded figure is '~206'; and the quoted 'verified robust at load average 123' -- no verdict contains that phrase, the recorded wordings being 'honest never went below 6 in seven runs, including at load 123' and "'cannot flake on a loaded machine' is no longer supported". Reviewers also report in prose to the parent agent and that prose is not archived, so I can only say these two are unattested, not that they are false -- which is exactly the point of saying so. Separately, the row states '202 orphaned `zsh` processes' and then 'an individual `kill -9 <pid>` in a loop killed all 201'; 202 and 201 are unreconciled in a row whose value is its counts.
findings.failure_scenario: The row's central argument is that recorded timing evidence was taken under conditions the recorder misread, and its persuasive force is that the load figures can be found in the artifacts. A session that fixes the leak, or that re-opens one of the findings the row says rests on this (the renew-rate floor, M4.41), greps `.harness/review/` for '206-213' or for 'verified robust at load average 123', finds neither, and cannot tell whether the row is quoting an unarchived prose report or inventing a number -- so it either discounts the whole row or re-litigates the M4.41 measurements from scratch. Fix: mark the paraphrases as paraphrases (or quote the verbatim '~206' and 'honest never went below 6 ... including at load 123'), and reconcile 202 against 201.

findings.summary: M4.45'S SUBSTANCE IS CORRECT AND UNDERSTATES THE DEFECT IT FILES. Verified against M4.1 (backlog-done.md:110): 'at three streams a broken sort still produced the asserted order about 1 run in 6 ... measured 8 of 8 fresh JVMs failing where the reviewer had measured 1 in 6 passing', so surviving 1 in 6 means failing ~5 in 6 and the comment's 'a broken sort would pass CI most times' is indeed the reciprocal. Verified that M4.8a (backlog-notes.md:321) states it the right way round in its own words, that 1/720 = 1/6! is consistent, and that no assertion is affected -- the six-key fixture at FakeSequencerTest.java:212-217 stands. Two imprecisions. (a) The backlog.md summary drops the comment's 'At three keys', leaving 'FakeSequencerTest says a missing sort produces the asserted order 1 run in 6' attached to a fixture that is six keys and 1 in 720; the notes row keeps the qualifier, the summary does not. (b) Both rows truncate the quotation before its sharpest half: the source comment (FakeSequencerTest.java:208-210) continues '; round-2 review measured exactly that', which attributes to a named review a measurement it did not make -- round-2 measured 1 in 6 PASSING, not 'passes most times'. That is the non-negotiable-4 half of the defect and neither row records it.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) A session reading backlog.md alone concludes the CURRENT six-key fixture escapes 1 run in 6, judges it too weak, and rewrites or re-fixtures a test that is already sound -- the row's own 'NO ASSERTION IS AFFECTED' finding lost in the summary that gets read first. (b) The eventual fix corrects the two clauses either side of the 'i.e.' and leaves 'round-2 review measured exactly that' standing next to the corrected text, where it now attributes the CORRECT statement to round-2 -- also false, and a second pass to find. This is the one-copy-fixed shape the row itself names.
